description: Scheduling and running about 410 pump stations, 2,300 center pivots, 18,000 drip zones, and 140 fertigation and chemigation skids across about 205,000 irrigated acres
process_owner: Vice President, Irrigation and Water Resources
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Crop water stress in hot, dry weeks (MTD 24 h in mild weather, 12 h in summer heat); fertigation and chemigation interlocks protect workers and water sources; flow records are the evidence for water permit reporting
source_evidence: EV-079 (Vice President, Irrigation and Water Resources interview); EV-067 (irrigated acres); EV-066 (revenue)
manual_workaround: Regional crews switch pumps and pivots to local (Hand) control at the panel under the written manual irrigation procedure; fertigation and chemigation stop until automation is verified; available staff can cover about 40% of pivots per day
dependent_systems: SYS-02; SYS-01 irrigation planning module; SYS-05; SYS-03
dependent_third_parties: Irrigation integrators INT-1 to INT-5; private APN carrier; pivot manufacturer cloud service (AQ-02); electric utilities
dependent_people_or_facilities: Irrigation Control Center Managers; about 380 irrigation technicians; 6 regional control centers; 410 pump stations
quantified_impact_basis: Yield and quality loss on stressed produce acres in a hot week (about 2% of the value of the affected crop per day) plus about $400,000 of overtime for manual operation
acquired_operation_dependency: AQ-02 pivots run through the pivot manufacturer's cloud service (see BP-18)
single_points_of_failure: SCADA master pair at DC-1 and DC-2; one carrier's private APN carries about 80% of field traffic

business_process: Freeze protection for strawberries and blueberries (December to February)
description: Overhead irrigation started at the trigger temperature on about 9,400 acres in R1, R3, and R4 on forecast freeze nights
process_owner: Vice President, Irrigation and Water Resources
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: An unprotected freeze night can destroy most open blooms and fruit in hours; the window between the trigger temperature and damage is short; staff fatigue across multi-night events
source_evidence: EV-079 (Vice President, Irrigation and Water Resources and Regional Farm Directors interviews); EV-067 (9,400 freeze-protection acres); EV-050 (freeze plans and drills)
manual_workaround: Freeze-night staffing plan: two-person crews at each freeze pump station start pumps by hand from thermometer readings; standalone temperature alarm dialers at each station
dependent_systems: SYS-02 (pump stations, weather stations, alarm path); SYS-05
dependent_third_parties: Electric utilities; private APN carrier; weather data service
dependent_people_or_facilities: Regional Farm Directors R1, R3, R4; about 160 trained freeze crew members
quantified_impact_basis: Loss of a large share of open bloom and fruit on 9,400 acres in one unprotected freeze night (per event, not per day)
acquired_operation_dependency: AQ-01 has 600 freeze-protected blueberry acres on a flat network
single_points_of_failure: Pump station PLCs and alarm path; limited night staffing

description: Dispatching harvest crews, recording piece-rate and hourly tally on rugged tablets, and lot assignment at the field
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Ripe produce must be picked within its harvest window; tally is part of the H-2A earnings record (20 CFR 655.122(j)(1)) and must be accurate for each payday
source_evidence: EV-079 (Chief Operating Officer interview); EV-070 (tally and payroll records); EV-066 (revenue)
manual_workaround: Paper tally cards keyed within 48 hours with second-person verification; crew leads record start and end times on paper
dependent_systems: SYS-01 (tally); SYS-06 rugged tablets; SYS-03
dependent_people_or_facilities: Crew leads (about 520 in season); up to 7,300 seasonal workers
quantified_impact_basis: About 20% of a peak day's harvest lost or downgraded plus about $600,000 of overtime and back-entry
acquired_operation_dependency: AQ-01 crews share tally tablet logins (EV-009)

description: Receiving, grading, packing, forced-air and hydro cooling, and case-level traceability labels at 17 packing sites
process_owner: Vice President, Packing and Cold Chain
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Fresh produce perishes within hours if not cooled; retailers reject unlabeled cases; traceability lot codes are assigned at initial packing (21 CFR 1.1320)
source_evidence: EV-079 (Vice President, Packing and Cold Chain interview); EV-067 (packing volumes); EV-066 (revenue); EV-072 (lot codes at initial packing)
manual_workaround: Packing lines run in manual mode with pre-printed lot label stock and paper lot logs; graders bypassed with hand grading at reduced speed (about 50% throughput)
dependent_systems: SYS-07 packing line software and label printers; SYS-01; SYS-12 order management; SYS-05
dependent_third_parties: Packing line and grader vendors (remote support); refrigeration service firms
dependent_people_or_facilities: About 2,400 packing staff in season; 17 packing sites
quantified_impact_basis: About 60% of a peak day's packed value delayed or lost; rejected loads and expedite costs
single_points_of_failure: Packing line management software (one instance per site, central configuration)

description: Temperature control and alarm monitoring in coolers, staging rooms, and loading docks
process_owner: Vice President, Packing and Cold Chain
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Temperature excursions over a few hours cause product loss and retailer claims; cold-chain records support customer audits
source_evidence: EV-079 (Vice President, Packing and Cold Chain interview); EV-055 (cold-chain monitoring SaaS)
manual_workaround: Hourly manual temperature checks recorded on paper; refrigeration controllers keep running on local setpoints
dependent_systems: SYS-07 refrigeration controllers and cold-chain sensors; cold-chain monitoring SaaS
dependent_third_parties: Cold-chain monitoring SaaS; refrigeration service firms; electric utilities
quantified_impact_basis: Product held in coolers at peak (about $16 million) at risk; assumes about 20% loss after an undetected 6-hour excursion

description: Customer orders, advance ship notices, load planning, and refrigerated carrier dispatch for retail and foodservice customers
process_owner: Vice President, Sales and Customer Operations
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About 1,900 truckloads a week at peak; retailers apply fines for missed ship windows and missing advance ship notices; volume commitments in supplier agreements
source_evidence: EV-080 (Vice President, Sales and Customer Operations interview); EV-067 (1,900 truckloads a week at peak); EV-058 (customer terms); EV-066 (revenue)
manual_workaround: Phone and email orders from the top 20 customers; manual bills of lading; carrier dispatch by phone
dependent_systems: SYS-12 EDI, order management, transport management; SYS-11 ERP
dependent_third_parties: EDI value-added network provider; refrigerated carriers; transport management SaaS
quantified_impact_basis: About 80% of a peak day's shipments delayed; retailer fines and spoilage

description: Produce Safety records, traceability lot data, and record retrieval for FDA, auditors, and customers
process_owner: Chief Food Safety and Quality Officer
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Records kept offsite must be produced within 24 hours of an FDA request (21 CFR 112.162(a); 112.166(a)); traceability records must be produced within 24 hours, as a sortable spreadsheet for FTL foods, once enforcement starts (21 CFR 1.1455(c)); customer trace-back requests during recalls
source_evidence: EV-079 (Chief Food Safety and Quality Officer interview); EV-071 (Produce Safety records); EV-072 (traceability readiness)
manual_workaround: Paper Produce Safety forms in each packing site's binder; latest monthly exports of FMIS records at each region
dependent_systems: SYS-01; traceability data service (Cloud provider A); SYS-07
dependent_people_or_facilities: Food safety managers at 17 packing sites; Traceability Program Manager
quantified_impact_basis: Audit and customer penalties; a missed FDA or customer trace-back request would be Severe for regulatory and reputation impact

business_process: Crop protection and nutrient application planning and records
description: Application recommendations, work orders, as-applied records, and Worker Protection Standard application and hazard information
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Application and hazard information must be displayed no later than 24 hours after an application ends (40 CFR 170.311(b)(5)); restricted-entry intervals protect workers
source_evidence: EV-079 (Vice President, Digital Agronomy interview); EV-071 (application records)
manual_workaround: Paper application logs and posted hazard information sheets at each farm's central display; spray work orders by phone
dependent_systems: SYS-01; SYS-09 as-applied data
dependent_third_parties: FMIS vendor; equipment dealers; Part 137 aerial application contractors
quantified_impact_basis: Delayed applications in pest windows and paperwork rework

description: GNSS auto-steer, RTK corrections, telematics, variable-rate seeding and spraying
process_owner: Director of Fleet and Precision Technology
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Planting and spraying windows are short; equipment can run with manual steering at lower accuracy and speed
source_evidence: EV-079 (Director of Fleet and Precision Technology interview); EV-024 (telematics and RTK)
manual_workaround: Manual steering at reduced speed; uniform-rate application; local RTK base stations operate without the network
dependent_systems: SYS-09; SYS-01
dependent_people_or_facilities: Equipment operators; 5 equipment and drone hubs
quantified_impact_basis: About 30% productivity loss across planting and spraying crews during peak windows

description: Weekly imaging flights and scouting reports that feed agronomy decisions and AI-001
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Imaging is weekly; scouting can switch to field walks
source_evidence: EV-079 (Vice President, Digital Agronomy interview); EV-054 (drone program)
manual_workaround: Field scouting on foot with paper or offline app notes
dependent_systems: SYS-10; Cloud provider B imagery pipeline
quantified_impact_basis: Scout overtime; delayed yield estimates

business_process: Grain and peanut drying and storage (harvest season)
description: Drying and aeration control for peanuts and field corn at 5 farms
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Wet peanuts and corn deteriorate within hours without drying; dryer fires are a safety risk
source_evidence: EV-079 (Chief Operating Officer interview); EV-068 (drying and storage on 5 farms)
manual_workaround: Dryers run on local panel controls with manual temperature checks every 2 hours
dependent_systems: SYS-08; SYS-05
quantified_impact_basis: Quality loss on wet product in dryers and trailers during harvest

business_process: Grower data platform for external growers (SL-1)
description: Agronomy analytics, irrigation scheduling recommendations, and yield reporting for about 420 contract and independent growers
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Contracted availability and confidentiality commitments to SL-1 clients; growers can irrigate on their own schedules for a day
source_evidence: EV-079 (Vice President, Digital Agronomy interview); EV-060 (SL-1 client agreements)
manual_workaround: Status page; email reports from the last good run; agronomists call key growers
dependent_systems: SL-1 platform (Cloud provider A); SYS-03
dependent_third_parties: Cloud provider A; messaging and notification service
quantified_impact_basis: Service credits to SL-1 clients and support surge
single_points_of_failure: Single cloud region for the platform front end (second region warm standby)

business_process: Grower packing, cooling, and traceability services (SL-2)
description: Packing, cooling, lot coding, and traceability data for about 160 contract growers at the 3 hubs
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Contract growers' produce perishes; their buyers rely on the hub's lot codes and traceability data; shares packing infrastructure with BP-04
source_evidence: EV-080 (Vice President, Grower Services interview); EV-060 (SL-2 grower agreements); EV-066 (grower services revenue)
manual_workaround: Same manual packing mode as BP-04; grower lots tracked on paper receiving logs
dependent_systems: SYS-07 at the 3 hubs; traceability data service; SYS-01
quantified_impact_basis: Service fees and grower claims for delayed packing
single_points_of_failure: Packing line management software at each hub

business_process: Payroll, timekeeping, and H-2A earnings statements
description: Weekly and biweekly payroll for up to 12,000 employees; earnings statements on or before each payday
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Earnings statements must be furnished on or before each payday (20 CFR 655.122(k)); wage payment laws; worker retention in season
source_evidence: EV-080 (Chief Human Resources Officer interview); EV-070 (payroll and H-2A records)
manual_workaround: Repeat the prior payroll through the payroll provider and correct from paper tally in the next cycle
dependent_systems: SYS-11; SYS-01 tally exports; SYS-03
dependent_people_or_facilities: Payroll team; Director of H-2A and Labor Compliance
quantified_impact_basis: Manual adjustments, penalties, and worker relations impact if payroll is late
acquired_operation_dependency: AQ-01 and AQ-02 employees still on legacy payroll until 2026-12-31

business_process: Labor planning and H-2A program administration
description: Crew plans, H-2A job order drafts, hours-offered tracking against the three-fourths guarantee, housing and transport assignments
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Hours offered must be recorded daily (20 CFR 655.122(j)(1)); crew plans drive transport and housing
source_evidence: EV-080 (Chief Human Resources Officer and Director of H-2A and Labor Compliance interviews); EV-070 (H-2A program records)
manual_workaround: Spreadsheet crew plans from the last export; daily hours-offered sheets by crew lead
dependent_systems: SYS-11; SYS-01; AI-006 crew planning optimizer (Cloud provider B)
dependent_people_or_facilities: Director of H-2A and Labor Compliance; regional labor coordinators
quantified_impact_basis: Planning overtime; risk of under-recorded hours offered

description: Quarterly and annual close, SOX controls, 10-Q and 10-K preparation
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: SEC filing deadlines at quarter-end (MTD drops to 48 h during the close window); SOX IT general controls
source_evidence: EV-080 (Chief Financial Officer and Controller interview); EV-046 (SOX IT general controls)
manual_workaround: Extend the close calendar; manual journal entries with dual approval
dependent_systems: SYS-11 ERP; data warehouse (Cloud provider B)
quantified_impact_basis: Overtime and audit fees; a late filing would be Severe

description: Seed, fertilizer, crop protection products, packaging, and parts ordering and inventory
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Farms hold about 7 days of inputs and packaging in season
source_evidence: EV-079 (Chief Operating Officer interview); EV-056 (supplier payments)
manual_workaround: Phone and email orders to the top 15 suppliers; paper receiving
dependent_systems: SYS-11 ERP
quantified_impact_basis: Expedite fees and packaging shortages after day 4

business_process: Farm operations at AQ-01 and AQ-02 (legacy systems)
description: Irrigation, tally, and records at the 13 acquired farms until integration
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Same drivers as BP-01 and BP-03; AQ-02 pivots depend on the manufacturer's cloud service (vendor states a 24-hour service restoration objective); AQ-01 local servers back up nightly (actual RPO 24 h)
source_evidence: EV-080 (Vice President, Integration Management Office interview); EV-069 (AQ-01 and AQ-02 profile); EV-033 (AQ-01 backups); EV-023 (AQ-02 pivot service)
manual_workaround: Manual pivot operation (AQ-02 crews trained 2026-06); paper tally
dependent_systems: AQ-01 farm servers and legacy directory; AQ-02 pivot cloud service and legacy directory
dependent_third_parties: Pivot manufacturer cloud service; AQ-01 local IT support firm
dependent_people_or_facilities: About 430 year-round and 1,250 seasonal workers at 13 farms
quantified_impact_basis: Water stress and harvest delays on about 40,000 acres
acquired_operation_dependency: Yes: AQ-01 and AQ-02 are the process
single_points_of_failure: Pivot manufacturer cloud service (AQ-02); AQ-01 farm servers (no tested restore)

description: Online subscriptions, weekly boxes, and pickup and delivery for about 38,000 subscribers
process_owner: Vice President, Sales and Customer Operations
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Weekly delivery cycle; subscriber personal information (no card data on company systems)
source_evidence: EV-080 (Vice President, Sales and Customer Operations interview); EV-061 (38,000 subscribers); EV-066 (revenue)
manual_workaround: Email subscribers; skip or credit one week
dependent_systems: E-commerce SaaS; payment processor hosted page
quantified_impact_basis: About one week of produce box revenue at risk if the outage spans a cycle

description: Flow meter data aggregation and reports to water management districts and state agencies
process_owner: Vice President, Irrigation and Water Resources
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Permit reports are monthly or annual; meter data is buffered in the field
source_evidence: EV-079 (Vice President, Irrigation and Water Resources interview); EV-013 (flow meters in the OT inventory)
manual_workaround: Manual meter reads at the meter face
dependent_systems: SYS-02 historian; farm data hub (Cloud provider A)
